items.content:
مباشر: البحرين تتهم إيران باستهداف "منشأة صناعية مدنية" والتحالف بقيادة السعودية يتصدى لهجمات حوثية
نشب حريق في منشأة صناعية بالبحرين جراء ضربة إيرانية السبت، وفق ما أعلنت المملكة التي استهدفتها أربعة هجومات منذ منتصف تشرين الثاني/نوفمبر، فيما تؤكّد طهران أنها تردّ على الضربات الأمريكية في ظلّ تصاعد حدّة النزاع في الشرق الأوسط. من جهته، أفاد ​التحالف الذي تقوده ​السعودية السبت بأنه اعترض ودمر ​صاروخا ‌باليستيا أطلقه الحوثيون باتجاه المنطقة ‌الغربية في المملكة، وسط تصاعد حدة التوتر بين السعودية والجماعة ​المتحالفة مع ‌إيران. تابعوا تغطيتنا المباشرة.

items.title: Israeli puts 'Gaza mosque crescent finial' up for sale, rights group says
items.content:
Israeli puts 'Gaza mosque crescent finial' up for sale, rights group says
An Israeli rights group has shared an image of an Israeli offering for sale a purported crescent finial from a mosque in Gaza's Rafah crossing.
In a post on X, Mistaclim said "a pious Jew" trades "in loot, in the spoils of war".
"Offers for sale for 2,500 shekels the moon at the end of the central mosque in the Rafah crossing and boasts that he has proof," the post read.
"And perhaps the problem lies in the rotten Israeli society, where the destruction of a place of worship is an opportunity for 'pride in the living room'."
"עברי חסיד" סוחר בביזה, בשלל מלחמה. מציע למכירה ב- 2,500 ש"ח את "הירח בסוף של המסגד המרכזי במעבר רפיח", ומתגאה שיש לו הוכחות. ו​אולי הבעיה בחברה הישראלית הרקובה בה חורבן של מקום תפילה הוא אפשרות ל"גאווה בסלון". https://t.co/W8lyTA9FWq

items.title: Labour MPs sign up for leadership course to counter rightwing populism
items.content:
Course run by former No 10 advisers is funded by Gary Lubner, who has given more than £11m to Labour
More than 20 Labour MPs have signed up to a year-long leadership course helping them to counter rightwing populism and deal with hostility, run by two former No 10 advisers and ultimately funded by multimillionaire donor Gary Lubner.
The training courses worth about £9,600 are being led by Ruth Turner, who was Tony Blair’s director of government relations, and Peter Hyman, who has worked for Blair, Keir Starmer and Andy Burnham’s governments.

items.title: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
items.content:
Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event
With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads.
On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs.

items.title: Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations
items.content:
The effects of the continent’s coming polls will be felt far and wide – and could well turn into ‘key tests’ of the bloc’s resilience
In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them.
Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it.

items.title: World Central Kitchen founder says three killed in Gaza strike 'not part of our team'
items.content:
World Central Kitchen founder says three killed in Gaza strike 'not part of our team'
The founder of the World Central Kitchen, Jose Andres, has said that the three people killed in an Israeli strike on a vehicle delivering food aid in Gaza, did not belong the organisation, nor did the vehicle.
In a post on X, Andres said, "Early reports linked them to World Central Kitchen. They were not part of our team, and it was not our vehicle. That's all we know."
"But here is what I do know. More than a year into a ceasefire, people in Gaza are still dying. Families are facing a fourth winter in tents," he added.
The Israeli army had earlier claimed in a post on X that it targeted three “Islamic Jihad terrorists” in a vehicle used to transport food and supplies to other group operatives in Gaza.
Andres added that a "ceasefire is not peace", calling upon leaders to work towards ending the conflict.
"To every leader with the power to change this, on every side: finish the work. End this war for good, so Palestinians and Israelis can live in safety, and so the people of Gaza can start to rebuild their homes, their schools, their kitchens," he said.
"Our teams, Gazans feeding Gazans, were cooking again today. They will be there tomorrow. A plate of food is hope. But it is not a future. Peace is."

items.title: Pro-Israel Hakeem Jeffries says he will push legislation targeting settler violence
items.content:
Pro-Israel Hakeem Jeffries says he will push legislation targeting settler violence
Pro-Israel US Democratic leader, Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to become the first Black speaker of the House of Representatives next year, has pledged to advance legislation targeting Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank within the first 100 days of the new Congress.
In an interview with The New York Times, Jeffries said the West Bank Settler Violence Protection and Prevention Act should be among the early legislative priorities, adding that he expected strong support for it within the House Democratic Caucus.
Jeffries also described the devastation inflicted on Palestinian civilians in Gaza as “unacceptable, unsustainable and un-American”, calling for increased humanitarian assistance, medical aid, housing support and access to clean water and air.
Asked whether he supported the proposed Block the Bombs and Stop the Settlements bills, which call for restricting arms sale to Israel and broader sanctions on settlement expansion, Jeffries said he had not taken a position.
On calls to halt US weapons exports used in regional conflicts, he said the current approach was “not sustainable” and needed to change.
More than a million people have signed a petition urging Democrats to reject Hakeem Jeffries as the next Speaker of the US House of Representative. An Economist/YouGov poll published last month found that Jeffries had just a 26 percent approval rating among registered voters.
Critics say that one reason Jeffries' popularity has taken a hit is that he is an avid supporter of Israel.
The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) ranks among his top campaign-financing contributors.
Jeffries said he expects strong support for the West Bank Settler Violence Protection and Prevention Act. (AFP)

items.title: Former UN envoy says Iran war was 'perfectly avoidable'
items.content:
Former UN envoy says Iran war was 'perfectly avoidable'
Iran war could have been avoided, Álvaro de Soto, a former UN special coordinator for the Middle East peace process, has said.
“It was perfectly avoidable. It need not have happened,” he said, adding that US officials have offered differing explanations for going to war.
Speaking at MED Dialogues conference in Naples, he said: “Lasting peace requires a willingness to confront the problems at the root of a conflict. Without addressing them, opportunities for peace will continue to be missed.”

items.title: Turkey says Israel could use Druze support to launch Syria operation
items.content:
Turkey says Israel could use Druze support to launch Syria operation
Israeli could use its support of the Druze to launch an operation in Syria, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said, warning that such an attack could lead to a wider conflict in the region.
In an interview with Turkish media, Fidan said Israel is providing military equipment and support to a Druze tribe in Syria, and may use that support to provoke the Syrian army and launch an attack.
Fidan said Turkey has discussed such the possibility of this operation with European and American officials.
The violence last year in Druze-majority Sweida - which began with clashes between Druze factions and Bedouin fighters in the southern province - left more than 2,000 people dead, including 789 Druze civilians, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights.
The Sweida violence also saw Israel launching air strikes in the province as well as in the capital Damascus, nominally in support of the Druze minority. In August, it struck a Syrian airbase where it said Turkey was planning to deploy forces.

items.title: Turkish foreign minister says Iran war fallout threatening global markets
items.content:
Turkish foreign minister says Iran war fallout threatening global markets
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said the economic burden brought by the US-Israel war is getting harder for many countries, while emphasising a ceasefire was needed to reverse global financial crises.
Speaking to Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, Fidan warned that the fallout from the conflict is threatening international markets.
“It is heading toward having very destructive effects,” he said.
Fidan said diplomatic efforts to re-open the Strait of Hormuz remain active, even though the process appears to be deadlocked, citing his recent discussion with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.
He also said that Ankara was keeping the humanitarian crisis in Gaza on the global radar permanently despite other international crises.
"In every speech, every initiative, and every platform wherever it may be, the Gaza issue is one we have not, and will not, allow to be forgotten," Fidan said.

items.title: Israeli occupation, Iranian interference threat to Lebanese sovereignty, Aoun says
items.content:
Israeli occupation, Iranian interference threat to Lebanese sovereignty, Aoun says
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has accused Iran of meddling in Lebanon's affairs through Hezbollah's weapons and also demanded Israel withdraw from the country's south.
In a speech on the eve of Lebanon's 83rd independence anniversary, Aoun vowed to press ahead with plans to bring all weapons under state control.
Lebanon's sovereignty still faces two threats, he said: "The Israeli occupation of parts of our territory" and foreign interference from "influential elements within the Iranian regime" through weapons and decisions outside the authority of the Lebanese state.
On Israel, Aoun stressed Lebanon's message was clear and direct: "Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks."
There would be "no occupation ever again", he said. "And no weapons outside the state that... serve the interests of, foreign powers," he added, without naming a specific group.
Such weapons may once have served a purpose, he said, but later imposed a high cost on Lebanon when they came to serve causes beyond its borders.
"You must hand over your weapons," Aoun said.
The Lebanese government has committed to disarming Hezbollah, whose arsenal has long outstripped that of the national army and which has justified its weapons as necessary to resist Israel.
In June, Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement that included the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual Israeli withdrawal from territories it occupies in the south and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area.
But implementation has stalled and Hezbollah has refused to surrender its weapons.
Israel's army still carries out strikes, shelling and detonations in the south, where its forces are operating in a self-declared "security zone" running around 10 kilometres.
Report by AFP

items.title: Pezeshkian says Iran engaged in 'silent economic war' as blockade completes 130 days
items.content:
Pezeshkian says Iran engaged in 'silent economic war' as blockade completes 130 days
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that his country was engaged in a "silent war that is far more difficult than the one in which missiles are launched and destruction is inflicted".
In a video shared by Al Jazeera, Pezeshkian said: "It is an economic war, one that you, as those working on the economic front, are dealing with. It is by no means an easy one."
While the Iranian economy has been under duress for years in the face of international sanctions, this year’s US naval blockade on Iranian oil and new sanctions imposed since the start of the war have increased the pressure manifold.
Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs, on Saturday described the naval blockade an act of war, vowing that the country would take action to break it, according to Mehr news agency.
On Saturday, the US Central Command said "today marks 130 consecutive days of America's blockade against Iran".
"US service members are enforcing the blockade with exceptional focus, determination, and professionalism — preventing Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps from exporting billions of dollars in crude oil," Centcom said on X.

items.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian homes in Hebron, Ramallah, set fire to vehicles
items.content:
Israeli settlers attack Palestinian homes in Hebron, Ramallah, set fire to vehicles
Israeli settlers attacked two Palestinian homes in the town of Yatta, south of Hebron, on Saturday evening, damaging property and attempting to break into one of the houses, Wafa reported.
Osama Makhmara, an anti-settler activist in southern Hebron, told Wafa that armed settlers attacked the home of Yusuf Shanaran in Wadi al-Rakhim, pelting it with stones and damaging its contents.
In a separate incident, settlers attempted to force open the door and smashed the windows of a home in Khallet al-Hummus area, south of Yatta.
Al Jazeera, meanwhile, reported that Israeli forces fired tear gas at Palestinians during a raid on the occupied West Bank town of Deir al-Sudan in the Ramallah area.
It said Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles and homes in the town northwest of Ramallah.
Israeli settler militias set fire to Palestinian vehicles and spray-paint anti-Palestinian slogans on Palestinian homes during an attack on the village of Kafr Malik, northeast of Ramallah, occupied West Bank. https://t.co/osfR8Mpf4p

items.title: In an Egypt village, generations of Palestinians denied a normal life
items.content:
Shamma Abu Hussein is possibly the last person in her village of refugees to have lived in historic Palestine. Living in Egypt, she has watched three generations of her family grow up in legal limbo.
She was among the hundreds of thousands who fled or were expelled during the creation of the State of Israel in 1948, whose descendants number in the millions.
Now she fears that the effects of the Gaza war and rhetoric from Israeli ministers calling for Gazans to be expelled means history is repeating itself.

items.title: Syrian Christian town demands security after resident kidnapped
items.content:
When Amina saw her nephew's motorbike knocked onto the ground and a car speeding away from his home in central Syria, she thought there had been a crash.
Instead, 38-year-old jeweller Maher Sankari had been kidnapped, an incident that plunged the Christian town of Suqaylabiyah into fear and prompted church leaders to demand authorities take action against repeated attacks and kidnappings of Christians.
Sankari's captors are demanding an eye-watering ransom of 120 kilogrammes (265 pounds) of gold.

items.title: Turkey says Israel blocking thousands of container homes from entering Gaza
items.content:
Turkey says Israel blocking thousands of container homes from entering Gaza
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said Israel is blocking thousands of container homes destined for Gaza, adding that Israeli authorities argue Hamas could use the metal structures  for manufacturing weapons.
Fidan told Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday that President Recep Tayyip Erdogan had ordered the temporary housing units, which Turkey used during the earthquake, to be sent to the Palestinian enclave.
He said Israeli restrictions were leaving displaced Palestinians dependent on fabric tents, exposing them to flooding, storms and cold weather.
“When floods, storms or cold weather come, they cause a disaster at least as devastating as hunger, if not more so,” he said.

items.title: ‘No time for a culture war’: Victoria’s electricity supply is at risk. Can it avoid power shortages and bill shocks?
items.content:
State faces electricity supply gap when Yallourn coal-fired power station closes in 2028 as experts warn neither Labor nor the Coalition has adequate plans
Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here
Victoria’s electricity supply will be at risk when a major power plant shuts in 2028 and neither major party is offering a plan at this month’s state election to deal with it, experts have warned.
All parties concede the giant Yallourn coal plant, which has operated in the Latrobe Valley since the 1970s and supplies a fifth of Victoria’s energy, is at the end of its functional life and will shut in less than two years. Analysts say the parties vying to run the state are failing to properly explain how they will fill the power shortfall the closure will create.

items.title: Hind Rajab Foundation urges Germany to arrest Israeli soldier over Gaza war crimes
items.content:
Hind Rajab Foundation urges Germany to arrest Israeli soldier over Gaza war crimes
The Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF) has urged Germany to arrest an Israeli soldier, Almog Keisi, who has been sighted in Luneburg this week, accusing him of war crimes, crimes against humanity and acts of genocide in Gaza.
In a statement, the foundation said it filed a criminal complaint with Germany’s Federal Public Prosecutor in Karlsruhe under the principle of universal jurisdiction set out in Section 1 of the German Code of Crimes against International Law that cover genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes.
German authorities can exercise jurisdiction over these offences regardless of the suspect’s nationality or where the alleged crimes were committed, the statement read.
HRF said that Keisi participated in the burning of residential buildings in Gaza City’s Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood between 9 and 10 October 2025, following the announcement of a ceasefire agreement and ahead of Israeli forces’ withdrawal from northern Gaza.
According to the complaint, Keisi posted photographs on 10 October showing himself placing explosives around civilian objects and later posing in front of buildings engulfed in flames. Other soldiers from the Givati Brigade also shared photographs of the burning structures, describing the destruction as a celebratory farewell.
HRF said it had geolocated the buildings near Al-Mawhobeen Secondary Female School and cited NASA fire-detection data and satellite imagery as corroborating evidence of the fires and damage.
Dyab Abou Jahjah, HRF’s general director, said: “Germany has received evidence against suspected war criminals before and chose to look away. Meanwhile, it arrests and prosecutes people for waving keffiyehs or chanting slogans against the genocide."
"So the question stands: how long will Germany spend its resources prosecuting those who fight the genocide instead of those who commit it?"

— The Hind Rajab Foundation (@HindRFoundation)

items.title: Gaza death toll rises to 1,671
items.content:
Gaza death toll rises to 1,671
Israeli attacks in Gaza killed at least nine people in the past 48 hours, taking the death toll since the October 2025 “ceasefire” to 1,661, Al Jazeera reported, citing the Palestinian health ministry.
The ministry said 55 Palestinians were wounded in the past 48 hours, and that the bodies of 851 people have been recovered. The total number of wounded since October 2025 has reached 6,062.

items.title: COP31 climate talks close to final deal, says summit president
items.content:
By Tuvan Gumrukcu and Ali Kucukgocmen
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) - UN climate talks in Turkey approached a final deal on Sunday with the announcement of a new package that COP31 presidents Australia and Turkey hope will achieve consensus on how to advance the fight against global warming.
The new draft deal was released two days after the conference in Antalya was scheduled to end.

Houthis deny threat to Saudi Arabia’s holy city of Mecca
items.content:
Houthis deny threat to Saudi Arabia’s holy city of Mecca
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said there was “no threat to Mecca” after Saudi Arabia issued a danger alert for the Mecca province and lifted it moments later.
In a statement on Telegram, Saree said that the “Yemeni people are ones who sanctify Mecca and all Islamic holy sites” and that “Saudi Arabia propagates a great lie by claiming there is a threat in the Mecca region. Our operations target its oil facilities and military bases.”

The Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Yemen's Houthis towards Saudi Arabia's western region, amid escalating hostilities between the kingdom and the Iran-aligned group.
Saudi Arabia's western coast hosts key energy infrastructure, including Yanbu South Terminal, a major crude-export facility linked to the East-West Pipeline, and the Jazan refinery in the country's far southwest.

A police officer who was shot outside a remote Tasmanian police station is alleged to have shot and killed his attacker in response to what authorities believe was a “targeted” incident.
Tasmania police deputy commissioner, Jonathan Higgins, said the sergeant Michael Preshaw had just come off shift at Whitemark police station on Flinders Island, which is north-east of the Tasmanian mainland. He had parked and gotten out of his police vehicle when he was shot at about 9.45pm on Saturday, Higgins told reporters on Sunday.

items.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's party for Israeli coalition talks
items.content:
Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's party for Israeli coalition talks
Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday.
Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the talks, scheduled to begin on Sunday, reflected a "genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government".
Former military chief Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc.
Saturday's announcement comes as Eisenkot's wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-led lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu's bloc.
"In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow," the party said in a statement.
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot speaks during a press conference at the President's office in Jerusalem on 8 November 2026 (AFP)

items.content:
إسرائيل: غادي آيزنكوت يدعو حزب بنيامين نتانياهو إلى مفاوضات لتشكيل ائتلاف حاكم
دعا حزب "يشار" بزعامة رئيس الوزراء الإسرائيلي المكلف غادي آيزنكوت، السبت، حزب "الليكود" الذي يقوده رئيس الحكومة المنتهية ولايته بنيامين نتانياهو، إلى إجراء جولة مباحثات لبمناقشة تشكيل ائتلاف حاكم. وأكد غادي آيزنكوت أن المباحثات المقرر أن تنطلق الأحد تعكس "التزاما حقيقيا بتشكيل أوسع حكومة ممكنة". ويأتي ذلك في ظل سباق مع المهلة الدستورية المتاحة لآيزنكوت قبل الشهر المقبل لكسر الجمود البرلماني. من جانبه، يلح نتانياهو على تشكيل حكومة وحدة وطنية، معتبرا إياها ضرورة لضمان أمن إسرائيل.

Iran’s Fars news agency reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) attacked two bases used by US forces in Bahrain, at Sheikh Isa and Juffair.

The report came after Bahrain earlier said that Iran targeted a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire and damage.

"As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control. items.title: Houthi attacks kill one civilian and injure seven in Taiz, Yemen government says
items.content:
Houthi attacks kill one civilian and injure seven in Taiz, Yemen government says
Houthi attacks on the besieged city of Taiz killed one person and wounded at least seven others, Yemen’s Office for Siege Affairs said.
The office said shelling hit an ambulance in the southern district of Sabr al-Muamad, killing one person and wounding six. The ambulance was reportedly taking part in an operation to rescue an injured civilian when it was hit.
Houthi snipers separately wounded a 20-year-old woman in al-Quhaf, south of the city, the office said.
Smoke billows from a site that was targeted during battles between Saudi-aligned Yemeni government fighters and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis at the Jabal Han front, west of the city of Taiz, on 21 October 2026 (AFP)

items.title: Houthi attacks killed 215 children since August, Yemen government says
items.content:
Houthi attacks killed 215 children since August, Yemen government says
Houthi attacks on government-held areas killed 215 children between 1 August and 15 November, Yemen’s internationally recognised government said.
Yemen’s ambassador to the United Nations, Abdullah al-Saadi, said the government recorded 3,334 violations against civilians and civilian objects during that period. He said the Human Rights Ministry also documented the deaths of 260 children recruited to fight for the Houthis over three and a half months.
Yemen’s Foreign Ministry said the Houthis exploited schools, pressured families and used summer centres and cultural and religious activities to recruit children.
“These practices constitute grave violations of the rules of international law concerning the protection of children in armed conflict,” the ministry said.
The ministry also recorded 93 attacks on educational facilities and said classes were suspended at 243 schools, affecting 137,000 students.

items.content:
Anticipating flood of Democratic requests, US president issues executive order in attempt to stymie oversight efforts
Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to an executive order issued late Friday.
The companies must also coordinate with the White House and US agencies on “appropriate responses” to any such requests, the order says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns, their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

items.title: Qatari delegation visits Tehran for talks, Iran says
items.content:
Qatari delegation visits Tehran for talks, Iran says
A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran on Friday night, an Iranian official said, as diplomatic efforts continued to end the war triggered by US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Tehran remained in contact with mediators, including Qatar, which has long used its ties with both Iran and the United States to help facilitate dialogue in regional disputes.
"We are in contact with mediators, including the Qataris, both in person and virtually, and are holding the necessary discussions to see whether another opportunity can be given to diplomacy," Gharibabadi said, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

Anthropic
has said that the
San Francisco
-based artificial intelligence (AI) company’s software has helped crack one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics – and experts say the claim checks out.
Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday
posted
a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.

items.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
items.content:
Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’
Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.
Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

items.title: Iran says it will take ‘any measure’ to break US blockade
items.content:
Iran says it will take ‘any measure’ to break US blockade
Iran’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi said he considers the economic blockade imposed by the US on Iran an act of war, Tasnim news agency reported.
“We consider the economic siege a hostile act, and we will take any necessary measures to break this economic siege,” Gharibabadi told Iranian reporters.
He also said that negotiations have not yet begun on Iran’s nuclear programme but that enriched materials will “under no circumstances” be exported from the country.

items.content:
A British endurance swimmer who swam in waters in the Strait of Hormuz to highlight the "devastating environmental consequences of war" on Saturday called for the waterway to be reopened and the pollution in it to be cleaned up.
"Oil tankers, gas carriers and other merchant ships are being attacked, day after day. The environmental consequences of this war will last for generations," Lewis Pugh wrote in a post on his website.

items.title: After outages hit US banks and aviation, FBI database reported hacked
items.content:
After outages hit US banks and aviation, FBI database reported hacked
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Sat, 11/21/2026 - 14:57
The database holds information on warrants and identities of fugitives, with experts warning that hackers could alter records relied on by police
FBI director Kash Patel is sworn in before testifying at a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, 15 September 2026 (Roberto Schmidt/AFP)
Off
The FBI is investigating a breach of its nationwide criminal information database, reported after a series of major technology disruptions in recent weeks.
The intrusion into the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which federal, state and local law enforcement agencies use to share criminal justice information, was discovered in recent days, CNN
reported
.
The FBI has called it a central law enforcement information system used by agencies across the country. The potential consequences extend beyond the theft of sensitive information.
A former FBI official who led investigations into cybercriminal groups said that officers rely on the database to identify fugitives, check outstanding warrants and access information.
“My concern isn’t simply whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an issue, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on,” the former official told CNN.
FBI director Kash Patel addressed the bureau's cybersecurity efforts on Fox News on Thursday, after officials had learned of the latest intrusion.
Patel touted
Operation Winter Shield
, an initiative launched earlier this year to encourage companies to strengthen their digital defences and protect sensitive information.
“Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said.
“We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.”
The FBI launched Operation Winter Shield in February as a cybersecurity campaign aimed at helping private-sector organisations strengthen their information technology and operational technology systems.
A week of outages
The FBI incident has unfolded alongside a series of technology disruptions affecting major US institutions.
On 13 November, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a
nationwide ground stop
after a technical problem disrupted its air traffic communications network,
grounding flights for several hours
.
US air travel thrown into chaos as nationwide flights grounded over 'radar instability'
Read More »
The disruption affected more than 18,000 flights, according to Reuters.
The FAA said the problem began when its legacy telecommunications system became unstable after receiving an unusually high volume of data through its network.
Days earlier, a
global outage
affecting Microsoft's services disrupted Outlook, Teams and its Copilot assistant, affecting organisations across several countries.
The outage affected businesses, banks, hospitals, courts, airlines and government agencies. Downdetector received reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.
On 16 November,
customers reported difficulties
accessing online services at several major US banks, including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and US Bank.
The following day, the National Security Agency's classified internal communications network, known as NSANet, also experienced an
outage
.

items.title: 'Will throw keys back to UN': Trump-appointed Board of Peace adviser says Israel blocking efforts
items.content:
'Will throw keys back to UN': Trump-appointed Board of Peace adviser says Israel blocking efforts
A senior adviser to the
US
-led Board of Peace for Gaza has said that the panel will "throw the keys back to the UN" if Israel continues to block efforts to prepare for an international stabilisation force and disarm Hamas.
“We have been extremely patient and have given Israel its space,” US official Josh Gruenbaum told the
Israeli
news site Ynet in an interview published on Friday.
But he said that it was “frustrating” that “Israel is failing to move forward on the commitments Prime Minister Netanyahu made to President Trump”.
“If this political leadership [in Israel] is now telling us that they no longer want to honour what they committed to, then just let us know now - and we’re basically going to throw the keys back to the UN to oversee the mandate,” Gruenbaum said.
Chaired by US President Donald Trump, the Board of Peace was
given
a sweeping mandate by the UN Security Council in November 2025 to establish an international stabilisation force in Gaza as part of a
20-point plan
to end hostilities and rehabilitate the devastated enclave.
While the plan features several Israeli demands, including the full demilitarisation of the Gaza Strip, talks have stalled for months amid
disputes
over Hamas’ weapons handover and ongoing Israeli attacks, which have killed over 1,600
Palestinians
in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire.

items.title: Trump claims he 'never cared' about regime change in Iran
items.content:
Trump claims he 'never cared' about regime change in Iran
US President Donald Trump has claimed that he "never cared too much about the regime" in Iran in an interview with Fox News on Saturday, discussing his strategy to end the current war.
Asked if he expects the Iranian government to outlast the current conflict, Trump said: "Some people said regime change, but you know, explain what that means, because really I've taken out two regimes already."
"You could call that the ultimate regime change," he added.
Trump also said that he was aiming to make a "permanent" deal with Iran that prohibited the Islamic Republic from developing a nuclear weapon.
"I'm going to make it so that if we have an incompetent president in four years or 15 years or 20 years, I'm gonna make a deal that is gonna be permanent. I'm not gonna let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon."

items.title: Virginia child dies in state’s first measles-associated death of 2026
items.content:
Death adds to national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years
Virginia
reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 ⁠on Friday, involving a child who tested positive for the infectious disease, the state’s health department said.
The department said the child was ⁠age four or younger. It did not disclose additional details, including the child’s vaccination status, citing the family’s privacy.

items.title: US denies Iran hit F-16 fighter jet
items.content:
US denies Iran hit F-16 fighter jet
The US has denied Iran's claims that the Islamic Republic's air defence systems hit an one of its F-16 fighter jets flying over the strait of Hormuz, forcing it make an emergency landing.
"Iran did not attack a U.S. F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday - at all," the US military Central Command (Centcom) posted on X on Saturday.
"All U.S. military fighter jets in the Middle East are safe and accounted for."
🚫 CLAIM: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims it targeted and damaged a U.S. F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday, forcing an emergency landing. This is FALSE. ✅ FACT: Iran did not attack a U.S. F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all. All U.S. military fighter jets in the Middle East are safe and accounted for.
— U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM)
November 21, 2026

items.content:
الجيش الجزائري يعلن القضاء على مُهربيْن مغربيَّي الجنسية "لم يمتثلا لأمر التوقف"
أفاد بيان لوزارة الدفاع الجزائرية، السبت، أن قوات حرس الحدود الجزائرية قتلت، الجمعة، شخصين يحملان الجنسية المغربية أثناء محاولتهما تهريب كمية من المخدرات عبر الشريط الحدودي المغلق بين البلدين في ولاية النعامة جنوب غرب الجزائر، وذلك بعد رفضهما الامتثال لأوامر التوقف. وتأتي العملية بعد أيام من تهديد الرئيس الجزائري عبد المجيد تبون باتخاذ إجراءات ضد مصنعي المخدرات في "المنبع"، معتبرا ذلك "دفاعا شرعيا عن النفس".

'Will throw keys back to UN': Trump-appointed Board of Peace adviser says Israel blocking efforts
items.content:
'Will throw keys back to UN': Trump-appointed Board of Peace adviser says Israel blocking efforts
Submitted by
Daniel Tester
on
Sat, 11/21/2026 - 13:27
The board said it was frustrated by Israel's obstructions while Gaza remains trapped in a deepening humanitarian crisis
Palestinians walk past destroyed buildings and displacement tents in Khan Younis, southern Gaza Strip, 17 November 2026 (Eyad Baba/AFP)
Off
A senior adviser to the
US
-led Board of Peace for Gaza has said that the panel will "throw the keys back to the UN" if Israel continues to block efforts to prepare for an international stabilisation force and disarm Hamas.
“We have been extremely patient and have given Israel its space,” US official Josh Gruenbaum told the
Israeli
news site Ynet in an interview published on Friday.
But he said that it was “frustrating” that “Israel is failing to move forward on the commitments Prime Minister Netanyahu made to President Trump”.
“If this political leadership [in Israel] is now telling us that they no longer want to honour what they committed to, then just let us know now - and we’re basically going to throw the keys back to the UN to oversee the mandate,” Gruenbaum said.
Chaired by US President Donald Trump, the Board of Peace was
given
a sweeping mandate by the UN Security Council in November 2025 to establish an international stabilisation force in Gaza as part of a
20-point plan
to end hostilities and rehabilitate the devastated enclave.
While the plan features several Israeli demands, including the full demilitarisation of the Gaza Strip, talks have stalled for months amid
disputes
over Hamas’ weapons handover and ongoing Israeli attacks, which have killed over 1,600
Palestinians
in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire.
Hamas formally
accepted
the Board of Peace’s roadmap in July, agreeing to hand over its weapons to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, a technocratic Palestinian body inaugurated and overseen by the US-led board.
But since then, Israel has continually refused to sign an agreement that would permit the stabilisation forces to deploy, and has blocked vetted members of Gaza’s police force from leaving the enclave to undertake training ahead of the planned weapons handover.
Israel has also refused to allow the construction of military outposts that would serve as barracks for the stabilisation force's troops, according to reports in
the Guardian.
Full text: 15-point draft peace plan between Hamas and Israel in Gaza
Read More »
“We are at a standstill due to political elements within the Netanyahu government, who have prevented us from progressing and from testing whether Hamas will keep its word,” Gruenbaum added.
Gruenbaum, a Jewish-American former private equity investor who also serves as a commissioner for the US government’s Federal Acquisition Service, was appointed by Trump in January to manage the day-to-day operations of the board, alongside the controversial diplomatic adviser
Aryeh Lightstone
.
Israel has killed over 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza since the Hamas attacks of October 2023 as the enclave faces an ongoing catastrophic humanitarian crisis, with 65 percent of its residents - around 1.4 million people - living in makeshift shelters or tents.
Many of these shelters were destroyed amid flooding earlier this month, which rights monitors called an “utterly preventable tragedy” fuelled by Israel’s ongoing blockade of the aid and supplies needed to repair vital infrastructure.
“A catastrophic winter is approaching for Gaza. We have already seen numerous headlines about flooding," Gruenbaum added in the Ynet interview.
"Israel needs to heed the international community’s call to avert this crisis."

items.title: SNL’s skit Sister captures the quiet agony of caregiving for women: ‘I’ve never felt seen like that’
items.content:
The viral satirization of the caregiving burden left to women and daughters hit home for many viewers
The
Saturday Night Live
sketch
, titled Sister quickly went viral this week for its satirization of the burden that women and daughters face to take care of aging family members. In the parody commercial, comedian John Mulaney touts the benefit of “Sister”, who he describes as “a live-in 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free, and also your sister” .
“Now I don’t have to worry about dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life, and the stuff I like to do,” Mulaney says, as the sister, played by cast member Jane Wickline, gives their father’s medication to him.
The sketch, which amassed over seven million views on YouTube in less than a week since it aired, has received thousands of responses and comments about its accuracy.
“This is one of the MOST wicked and spot on SNL sketches ever written,” wrote one commenter on YouTube. Another posted: “As a hospice nurse this definitely tracks. I deal 90% of the time with adult daughters, and if there is no daughter, it is the daughter in law.”
“This is so real it almost gave me a stroke from rage,” added another viewer.

shot and wounded
by immigration officers as they arrested him in
New York
in October.
The US district court judge Hector Gonzalez said in a written ruling that agents may have made a procedural error in serving an arrest warrant on Oscar Belgal before he was given a notice to appear in immigration court. However, he wrote, that was merely a technical error that does not require Belgal to be released from federal custody pending deportation proceedings.

The Israeli military said its forces had been targeting Islamic Jihad militants in the area at the time and that the vehicle had been transporting food to members of the organisation.

items.title: COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime
items.content:
By Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The COP31 climate summit will either produce a good deal or no deal at all, the European Union's top climate official said on Saturday as talks stretched deep into overtime.
Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, delaying an agreement at the two-week conference that had been scheduled to end on Friday.

items.title: ‘Hell dorm’: Florida prisoners testify about 119F heat indexes and walls that sweat
items.content:
Temperatures in a concrete facility contributed to one man’s death after he struggled to breathe, prisoners allege
On Tuesday afternoon Dwayne Wilson, 69, a thin Black man dressed in a light gray prison uniform, testified about the stifling heat he experienced in the Dade correctional institute, a concrete state prison south of Miami,
Florida
, without air conditioning. He removed his glasses and wiped his eyes as he spoke. “It was so hot,” he said, his voice catching. “It’s so hot sometimes you have to put water on the floor just to try to keep cool.”
Wilson said he’s housed in the H dorms, a T-shaped building with one-to-two-person cells, nicknamed “hell dorm” by prisoners because its concrete walls radiate heat absorbed from the sun. The plaintiff’s law firm, the
Florida Justice Institute
, convinced a judge to allow 31 sensors to be temporarily installed throughout the prison during the summer of 2025. They recorded temperature and humidity levels that
Stefano Shiavon
, a professor of civil and environmental engineering with expertise in thermal comfort, used to calculate the heat index. He found it to be above 88F (31C) 97% of the time, with the highest heat indexes often recorded at night, including one reading in the H dorm dayroom equivalent to 119F (48C) at 10pm one July day last year. “The walls sweat,” Wilson said. “It’s miserable in the cell at night because, again, it’s so hot. No air comes to the bed we sleep at and the bed is soaked in sweat.”

items.title: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
items.content:
Moscow intelligence thought to be behind plan to kill musician Kyivstoner before concert in Denmark
Denmark’s foreign minister has said Russia’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Moscow was suspected of being behind an attempted killing of a US-Ukrainian rapper.
“We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark,” Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. The expulsion will happen within seven days.

items.title: Iran claims to have struck US F-16 jet
items.content:
Iran claims to have struck US F-16 jet
Iran
's army has claimed that its air defence systems struck a
US
F-16 fighter jet with a missile on Friday evening, damaging the aircraft.
Iranian state media reported that the strike forced the plane to divert course and make an emergency landing.
The US military, which has seen few casualties throughout the war, has not commented on the incident.
This is a developing story. We'll bring you more updates when we get them.

items.title: الله اكبر
items.content:
الله اكبر

مشاهد من استهداف طائرة اف 16 الامريكية يوم امس في الاجواء الايرانية

الجيش الايراني: في مساء يوم الجمعة، تمكنت أنظمة الدفاع الجوي المحلية التابعة للجيش، المنتشرة في جنوب البلاد، والتي تخضع لسيطرة الشبكة الموحدة للدفاع الجوي في البلاد، من تحديد موقع طائرة مقاتلة من طراز F-16 أمريكية فوق الخليج العربي.

خلال هذه العملية، وبعد اعتراض الطائرة الأمريكية من طراز F16، قامت الأنظمة الدفاعية بإطلاق صاروخ باتجاهها. ونتيجة لانفجار الصاروخ بالقرب من الطائرة، تعرضت الطائرة الأمريكية المهاجمة لأضرار، واضطر طيارها إلى إلغاء المهمة والهبوط الاضطراري في أحد أقرب المطارات في المنطقة.

items.title: US pursuit of ‘Trump-class’ warships has blown cost of new fleet by billions, report warns
items.content:
Iran war stretching fleet’s capacity, navy chief admits, as CBO finds estimated cost of new ships ‘unrealistically low’
The US navy’s commitment to the new Trump-class battleships has blown out the cost of its new fleet by billions of dollars, a report to the US Congress has found, as the acting secretary of the navy conceded this week the Iran war was “stretching” the fleet’s capacity.
The challenges facing the world’s biggest naval force were highlighted this week, when the return of the USS George Washington from the Middle East on Wednesday ended a rare three-month period when the US had no aircraft carrier across all of the Pacific. Deployments have been regularly running beyond 300 days, with the maintenance and repair of ships deferred so they can stay at sea longer.

items.title: ‘Music was our teacher’: the sound system pioneers reviving the scene in Manchester and beyond
items.content:
Manchester-based Megatone Sound Foundation and Baron Turbo Charge have rejuvenated the culture to offer a sense of belonging and empowerment
For a generation of young Black Mancunians, some of the history lessons that mattered most were not taught in classrooms, but through towering stacks of amps and speakers, turntables and Jamaican records.
“We didn’t know where we fit in. We didn’t know our history. Our parents were busy working two or three jobs,” says Errol “Barzy” Beaumont, a founder member of Baron Turbo Charge, Manchester’s long-running reggae sound system. “It was the records – Burning Spear, Bob Marley,
Culture,
that were telling us about our culture, which wasn’t on the school curriculum. For us, the sound system was not just entertainment – it was an education.”

items.title: Iran says new air defence system intercepted US Reaper drone over Hormuz
items.content:
Iran says new air defence system intercepted US Reaper drone over Hormuz
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Sat, 11/21/2026 - 09:50
The US reported losing at least 45 Reaper drones by August, while Iran says its forces have now destroyed 58 since the war began
A crew member monitors an MQ-9 Reaper military drone at Cognac air base in Chateaubernard, southwestern France, 12 June 2026 (Christophe Archambault/AFP)
Off
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it shot down a
US
MQ-9 Reaper drone in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported on Saturday.
The IRGC
said
it is the 58th aircraft destroyed by
Iranian
forces since the start of the war, adding that the drone was detected, tracked and destroyed by Iran’s new air defence system.
In August, the US military
said
that it had lost at least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones during the war, amounting to roughly a quarter of its fleet, according to three US officials cited by The Washington Post.
The newspaper estimated the losses could represent more than $1.3bn in equipment costs.
The development comes amid renewed tensions between Washington and Tehran, with attacks on commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.
A commercial tanker was hit by an unknown missile about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab port in Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO)
said
.
The US military
said
on Tuesday that it had
attacked a missile launching site
on Iran’s Qeshm Island in retaliation for attacks by Iran on US personnel and property.
Iran later
said
it had attacked US drone and missile facilities at the Ali al-Salem air base in Kuwait.
US builds up forces around Iran, but can it sustain another war?
Read More »
Kuwait reported responding to "hostile drone activity", while Bahrain said it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks.
The conflict, launched by the US and Israel on 28 February, has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
The strait is one of the world's most important energy corridors. In 2025, around 25 per cent of world oil trade by sea was
carried
through the Strait of Hormuz.
A memorandum of understanding was signed in June between the two nations
to continue dialogue
about issues such as free passage within the strait, Iran’s nuclear and missile capabilities and sanctions.
The agreement did not produce a lasting settlement, and the parties have continued to disagree over maritime security and the terms of a broader deal.
Blockade and negotiations
Washington has stepped up economic pressure on Tehran as the two sides remain at odds over the conditions for ending the war and restoring navigation through the strait.
The US Treasury has
imposed sanctions
against four people for acting as "oil trustees" and facilitating the movement of revenues from international sales of Iranian oil in order to help Tehran avoid sanctions and the US-imposed blockade.
Mossad abducted Iranian general in Turkey, tortured him for weeks before killing him: Report
Read More »
Those hit by the sanctions include the former intelligence officer of the IRGC, Mohammad Javad Bavand, and Majid Taj, brother of the president of the Iranian Football Federation, Mehdi Taj.
Under these sanctions, all assets held by the individuals in the US are frozen. Additionally, none of these individuals can conduct business with individuals or companies based in the US, unless in compliance with relevant regulations and authorisations.
The blockades began on 13 April. US Central Command has
said
it will block sea traffic to and from Iranian ports and waters. However, ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz to and from ports outside Iran will be allowed to pass unhindered.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi
said
on Friday that the blockade must be broken to allow the country to resume oil exports.
“We are making every possible effort regarding oil exports and negotiations. The naval blockade must be broken,” he told reporters in Tehran.
Araghchi has also said Iran’s seven conditions must be met before the Strait of Hormuz can reopen. The demands include an end to the war and the lifting of sanctions and the US blockade, according to his recent statements.
He said Tehran was prepared to discuss how the conditions could be implemented, but that negotiations depended on Washington taking confidence-building measures.

items.title: Iran says it downed US drone over Qeshm Island
items.content:
Iran says it downed US drone over Qeshm Island
Iran’s
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps
has said that it has destroyed a US Predator drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
The US
claimed
that its fighter jets used "precision munitions” to strike an Iranian missile site on the island last Tuesday.
Qeshm is the largest island in the Gulf and is seen as strategically significant, given its position at the gateway of Hormuz.

items.title: Black Friday deals for liquid Brazilian butt lifts criticised over safety fears
items.content:
Experts say BBLs and other cosmetic procedures can be risky and seasonal offers at clinics in England could make people rush decisions
Clinics in England are promoting seasonal deals – including for Black Friday – on liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), despite concerns about the risks of the procedure.
The
government is consulting on limiting liquid BBLs
, vampire facials and deep chemical peels in England to qualified healthcare professionals. The proposals follow the death of Alice Webb, a 33-year-old mother of five, after a botched liquid BBL in a Gloucester salon in 2024. Her family have
called for laws against “cosmetic cowboys”
to be introduced before more people die.

items.title: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
items.content:
Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation
A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.
In 2024, as the surrounding city was
almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs
, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was
forced to play its World Cup qualifying games abroad
.

items.title: Explosive-laden boxes dropped from the sky: Israel’s latest weapon in Gaza
items.content:
Explosive-laden boxes dropped from the sky: Israel’s latest weapon in Gaza
Jaber Yaseen's family was preparing the traditional maftoul dish for their Friday family lunch when they heard a loud engine approaching.
The Palestinian family of 13 were startled by the noise, which grew louder as it approached their home in the al-Zaytoon neighbourhood, east of Gaza City.
“I thought it was an Israeli tank at first. I looked out of the window and was shocked to see a huge quadcopter drone carrying two boxes of explosives, flying low over our neighbourhood,” Yaseen told Middle East Eye.
“I watched the drone move towards us. Without any warning, it dropped the two boxes of explosives onto our roof. I was terrified for my children's lives. I grabbed them and rushed out of the house, knowing the explosives could detonate at any moment. We couldn't take anything with us.”
Panic spread as families watched more Israeli drones dropping explosives onto rooftops across the neighbourhood. Dozens were forced to flee their homes, with nowhere to go.

items.title: Iran seeking 'good, honourable and dignified agreement': Araghchi
items.content:
Iran seeking 'good, honourable and dignified agreement': Araghchi
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said that Iran remains open to diplomacy with the US but is seeking a “good, honourable and dignified agreement”.
In an interview with Iranian state newspaper Iran Daily, published on Saturday morning, Araghchi added that Iran saw giving up its enriched uranium as a "red line" in negotiations, and dismissed suggestions that Tehran would change this policy.
Araghchi was part of an Iranian delegation that visited Oman and Pakistan this week for talks to end the country's war with the US and Israel, which has now lasted over eight months.

items.title: Explosive-laden boxes dropped from the sky: Israel’s latest weapon in Gaza
items.content:
Explosive-laden boxes dropped from the sky: Israel’s latest weapon in Gaza
Submitted by
Abdallah al-Naami
on
Fri, 11/20/2026 - 12:08
Palestinian families recount how Israeli quadcopters drop explosives on to their homes, demolishing entire buildings and displacing dozens of families
Jaber Yaseen stands amid the rubble of his home, destroyed by explosive-laden boxes dropped by an Israeli drone in Gaza City’s al-Zaytoon neighbourhood (Abdallah al-Naami/MEE)
Off
Jaber Yaseen's family was preparing the traditional maftoul dish for their Friday family lunch when they heard a loud engine approaching.
The
Palestinian
family of 13 were startled by the noise, which grew louder as it approached their home in al-Zaytoon neighbourhood, east of Gaza City.
“I thought it was an Israeli tank at first. I looked out of the window and was shocked to see a huge quadcopter drone carrying two boxes of explosives, flying low over our neighbourhood,” Yaseen told Middle East Eye.
“I watched the drone move towards us. Without any warning, it dropped the two boxes of explosives on to our roof. I was terrified for my children's lives. I grabbed them and rushed out of the house, knowing the explosives could detonate at any moment. We couldn't take anything with us.”
Panic spread as families watched more
Israeli
drones dropping explosives on to rooftops across the neighbourhood. Dozens were forced to flee their homes, with nowhere to go.
A group of residents gathered at a distance, watching as the quadcopter drones continued to drop explosives. Minutes later, the devices on the rooftops began detonating.
For 33-year-old Ismail Madi, watching the drones was heartbreaking.
“We had been displaced several times before, and each time I held on to some hope that we would return home. But when I saw the quadcopter drones carrying explosives above our home, I felt as though I had left my soul behind as I walked away,” Madi told MEE.
Abdaljawad Badwan, another resident of the neighbourhood, described the terror of watching the attack unfold.
“Everyone was shocked and terrified. Every time an explosion went off, we hoped it would be the last. But the drones kept coming back with more boxes.”
Three multi-storey houses were destroyed in the attack on 13 November 2026 (Abdallah al-Naami/MEE)
Families told MEE that the initial explosions were intended to create openings in the roofs.
Large quadcopter drones, measuring approximately 4m across, then continued to drop nearly 60 boxes of explosives inside each house.
The explosives were subsequently detonated, destroying the houses and damaging many surrounding buildings.
By 10pm (8pm GMT), the Israeli attack on 13 November had completely demolished three multi-storey houses and severely damaged dozens of others.
Nearly 33 families lost their homes that night.
Forced into the streets
With their homes destroyed, Palestinian families were left without shelter in the cold night.
“We had nowhere to go for shelter. All 13 of us spent the night on the pavement. We are still living on the pavement in a makeshift tent that I built the following day,” Yaseen said.
The sudden displacement has compounded the suffering these families were already enduring.
“We spent the night on the street, surrounded by piles of rubbish, rodents and insects. My two-year-old son, Abdalsamad, was very sick, and I had to go around asking neighbours for painkillers late at night,” said Badwan, a father of four.
'I built this home brick by brick. I don't know how to describe what I feel'
-
Jaber Yaseen, Gaza resident
In the early hours of the morning, families returned to inspect their homes. They were confronted with scenes of devastation.
“I have lived here my entire life, yet I could barely recognise my neighbourhood because of the sheer scale of destruction,” Madi said.
For him, the aftermath was particularly devastating. He had married just two months earlier.
“I put a lifetime of hard work into preparing my home and saving for my wedding. I had hoped to begin a new chapter of my life there, with a sense of stability and safety. I was overwhelmed with grief when I saw my home and everything I had worked for destroyed before my eyes,” Madi told MEE.
Standing amid the rubble of his home, Yaseen struggled to put his feelings into words.
“I built this home brick by brick. I don't know how to describe what I feel. It's heartbreaking. I find myself crying every night just thinking about my home,” he told MEE.
‘We face death every day’
Since returning to their neighbourhood following the October 2025 ceasefire agreement, families in al-Zaytoon have faced a daily struggle for survival.
Being located near the so-called "Yellow Line" - a military boundary imposed by Israeli forces inside the Gaza Strip - has meant a consistent threat from Israeli soldiers nearby.
“We face death every day,” Madi told MEE.
“The Yellow Line is just 50m away. Israeli quadcopter drones and tanks come every day and open fire towards our homes. These attacks have become part of our daily routine. We have no choice but to adapt. We have even taught the children how to hide when the shooting starts.”
Israel’s expanding ‘Yellow Line’ swallows Gaza districts and uproots families
Read More »
Israeli forces have steadily pushed the "Yellow Line" westwards over the past year, encroaching on residential areas, often without warning.
“We have lived in constant danger for the past year. We could wake up any day to find that the [Israeli] army has moved the yellow blocks westwards, past our homes, and that we have to evacuate,” Yaseen said.
The daily attacks are not the only hardship these families face. Living in an area classified as dangerous by humanitarian aid organisations, they receive little to no assistance.
Families say that the nearest source of water, medical centre or school is 2km away. Adults and children must make the dangerous journey every day, despite the recurring Israeli attacks.
“We have adapted to the daily Israeli attacks and the lack of aid because we wanted to stay in our homes. The quadcopter attack was shocking. I never imagined something like this could happen, especially without any warning,” Yaseen said.
A new tactic to displace families?
Despite the so-called ceasefire in Gaza, Israel has continued its attacks in Gaza, killing at least 1,600 Palestinians, destroying homes and expanding its control through military force.
Last week's attack on al-Zaytoon neighbourhood marked a new development, with Israeli forces using quadcopter drones to plant boxes of explosives inside homes in a populated area outside the "Yellow Line". Families had barely enough time to escape before watching their homes being destroyed.
The attack was not an isolated incident.
'I was born and raised in this home. I cannot live away from it'
- Ismail Madi, Gaza resident
Over the past week, Israel has escalated its use of quadcopter drones carrying boxes of explosives, destroying Palestinian homes and property outside the "Yellow Line" in al-Maghazi, al-Musadder, Khan Younis and al-Nuseirat.
As these attacks grow in intensity and frequency, families across Gaza fear that explosive-laden quadcopter drones are becoming a central part of Israel's tactics to destroy what remains of Palestinian homes in Gaza and forcibly displace residents.
“We are worried that Friday's attack was a message or a threat from the [Israeli] army telling us to leave the area, and that perhaps we won't be allowed to return to it in the near future,” Yaseen told MEE.
On Thursday, for the first time since the so-called ceasefire, Israel announced the launch of a ground attack outside the "Yellow Line" in al-Nuseirat, in central Gaza.
During the preceding night, Israeli forces destroyed several buildings in northern al-Nuseirat using boxes of explosives planted by quadcopter drones.
Despite the destruction, Ismail Madi returns to his home, which he sees as the community’s first line of defence (Abdallah al-Naami/MEE)
But despite the destruction of their homes and the catastrophic conditions they face, families were quick to return to al-Zaytoon neighbourhood after the attack.
“I spend the day here in the neighbourhood. My soul is attached to my home, even though it is now just a pile of rubble,” Yaseen told MEE.
“I'll build my tent here, next to the remains of my home. I'd rather die than live away from home.”
For Madi, returning to the neighbourhood is about more than his attachment to his home.
“I was born and raised in this home. I cannot live away from it,” he told MEE.
“By staying here in the neighbourhood, we are the first line of defence for the community. Our steadfastness gives other families living near the Yellow Line a sense of hope and safety.”

items.title: UK, France and China vote against UAE's Lana Nusseibeh at UN
items.content:
UK, France and China vote against UAE's Lana Nusseibeh at UN
Lana Nusseibeh's bid to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations suffered a setback on Friday after the
UK
,
France
and
China
all voted against the Emirati diplomat in the latest informal straw poll conducted to help determine who should replace Antonio Guterres.
Along with the
US
and
Russia
, the countries make up three of the P5, the permanent members of the UN Security Council that can veto any prospective candidate for the world body's top job.
While votes in the straw poll are cast anonymously, diplomatic and other sources close to the Security Council told Middle East Eye that the UK, China and France were the P5 members who had voted to "discourage" Nusseibeh's candidacy.
The US, Russia and Israel - which is not currently part of the Security Council and thus does not vote - all back Nusseibeh, according to the same sources.
In total, the
UAE
minister of state and former ambassador to the UN received seven "encourage" votes, six "discourage" votes and two "no opinion" votes - the same result she achieved in the last straw poll, held on 6 November.
Read more: UK, France and China vote against UAE's Lana Nusseibeh at UN

items.title: Fire at power station in Iraq's Basra kills at least 4, injures 35
items.content:
BASRA, Iraq, Nov 21 (Reuters) - At least 4 people were killed and 35 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.
Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.
The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.

minister of state and former ambassador to the UN received seven "encourage" votes, six "discourage" votes and two "no opinion" votes - the same result she achieved in the last straw poll, held on 6 November.
Candidates need to secure at least nine votes to then be put forward to the UN General Assembly, but in order for this to happen they need to have no "discourage" votes.
British MPs urge government to block UAE's Nusseibeh from top UN job
Read More »
The frontrunner, the Costa Rican economist and diplomat Rebeca Grynspan, has 10 encourage votes, but two discourage votes from members of the P5, believed to be Russia and the US.
Argentina's Rafael Grossi, who is backed by his country's far-right president Javier Milei and is favoured - like Nusseibeh - by the US, also picked up three discourage votes from members of the P5.
With no agreement among the P5, the process remains deadlocked.
Nusseibeh has vowed to stay in the race,
posting
on X: "I remain fully committed to this campaign and will continue engaging Member States to earn their support and make the case for a more active, results-focused and responsive United Nations."
Lobbying from the UAE
The results remain a setback for the Abu Dhabi-born diplomat, who has been relentless in her pursuit of the job despite fierce opposition from civil society focused mainly on her country's involvement in the war in
Sudan
.
In her official role in the UAE's government, Nusseibeh has denied reports from the UN Panel of Experts on Abu Dhabi's sponsorship of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary force found to have committed genocide in Darfur
by the UN
and the
US
.
On Friday, MEE reported on efforts she had made to lobby Iain Duncan Smith, after the former leader of the UK's Conservative Party
spoke out in parliament
about the UAE's “sponsoring of a huge amount of terrorism in
Sudan
” and called on the British government to use its Security Council veto to block her nomination.
Exclusive: UAE's Nusseibeh lobbied UK's Iain Duncan Smith over UN candidacy
Read More »
The former government minister told MEE that in his meeting with Nusseibeh he reiterated the position he had taken in parliament about the UAE’s involvement in Sudan - denied by Abu Dhabi - and called for the release of “two British citizens wrongly held in Dubai:
Ryan Cornelius and Charles Ridley
”.
Duncan Smith told Nusseibeh that the UAE needed to “cease and desist” from its involvement in the Sudan war.
He told Nusseibeh that her UN candidacy gave the UAE a chance to do the right thing and withdraw from the war in Sudan and release Cornelius and Ridley, two British citizens who have been detained in Dubai for almost 20 years.
“They are corrupt, and they are corrupting,” Duncan Smith said of the Emiratis, before calling on UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to "take a stand".
It would appear that this stand has been taken by Britain, as well as France and China. Nusseibeh and the UAE remain committed to her candidacy, though, and can use what one former British government official described to MEE as "money and investment" as leverage.
Responding to MEE's request for comment on Friday, a spokesperson for Nusseibeh’s campaign said: “Lana Nusseibeh is meeting a wide range of stakeholders as part of her candidacy for UN secretary-general.
"We do not comment on the content of private meetings. Lana has taken a leave of absence from her ministerial role since the submission of her nomination. She took this decision as part of her genuine commitment to the independence of her campaign and potential future role.”

items.title: Pro-Palestine activist Fergie Chambers released, says 'my sacrifice is very small'
items.content:
Pro-Palestine activist Fergie Chambers released, says 'my sacrifice is very small'
Spain's High Court has released pro-Palestinian activist and US media heir Fergie Chambers on conditional bail, while it considers an extradition request by the US, according to a court ruling released on Friday.
The court said it had decided to release Chambers after US authorities acknowledged what they described as substantial and unintentional errors in the Spanish translation of an FBI agent's sworn statement submitted in support of the extradition request.
On his release, Chambers told Reuters he believed the accusations against him were baseless and politically motivated, adding that he had been alone in a cell for what "felt like a long time".
"I'm glad that this is a step in the right direction," he said.
Chambers added: "At the end of the day, I understand that most of the sacrifice I've had to make is very, very small in relation to the struggle that we are all a part of for the Palestinian people, for their liberation, for their sovereignty, for their respect, for the right to live."
"But in the context of just being alone in a cell all the time, it feels like a long time. I just missed my family. I really missed my family and my friends,” Chambers said.
Chambers, whose family owns Cox Enterprises, was arrested at the request of US authorities on 10 July while on holiday in Ibiza. He has been held in custody ever since on accusations including riot, conspiracy to commit riot and international money laundering. Chambers, whose full name is James Cox Chambers Jr, denies wrongdoing.
Separately, Chambers' lawyers said they were challenging a raid by Irish police on his family home in Dublin, which they said was conducted at the request of US authorities and involved the seizure of electronic devices and other property. His legal team said it would seek judicial review unless authorities clarify the legal basis for the operation.
Report by Reuters
Chambers said his sacrifice was very small in relation to the struggle for the Palestinian people (Reuters)

items.title: Morning update
items.content:
Morning update
Good morning, Middle East Eye readers,
If you are just joining us, here are the key developments from across the region and beyond:
* Saudi-led coalition forces say they have intercepted and destroyed several Houthi missiles and drones headed towards Saudi Arabia.
* Six Palestinians were killed and several others injured in Israeli strikes and gunfire across Gaza since Friday.
* Iran still has hope that diplomacy can end its war with the US, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said, adding that the two sides are still exchanging messages through mediators.
* A Palestinian man was killed by Israeli forces near Ramallah on Friday as forces carried out raids, detentions and a home demolition across the occupied West Bank. Several Palestinians were also wounded in attacks by settlers and forces in the occupied territory.
* US Vice President JD Vance on Friday declined to say whether he would have authorised strikes on Iran to stop it developing a nuclear weapon, sidestepping US President Donald Trump’s calls for him to say the attacks were necessary and that he would carry them out again.
* Trump has said the International Criminal Court was "out of control", while claiming China "agreed for the first time to condemn the abuses and overreach" of the court, AFP reported.
* Air strikes have targeted Mokha and al-Shamayatayn districts in Taiz governorate of Yemen, Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reports.
* The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has said six attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz were reported in the past week, while shipping traffic remained about 65 percent below pre-war levels.
* Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its aerospace forces have shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, state broadcaster Irib reported.
* A senior adviser to the Trump-appointed Gaza Peace Council has warned that the body could return responsibility for the enclave to the United Nations if Israel does not honour its commitments under the 20-point plan, Israeli outlet Ynet has reported.

items.title: Fire at Iraqi power station leaves four dead, 30 injured
items.content:
Fire at Iraqi power station leaves four dead, 30 injured
At least four people were killed and 30 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.
Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.
The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.
The Hartha station has an installed generating capacity of 800 megawatts but had been operating at around 400 megawatts before the fire, they said.
There was no immediate official information on the cause of the fire or the extent of the damage, INA reported.
Report by Reuters

items.content:
Seven Gazans wounded, one critically, in Israeli gunfire and air strikes
Seven Palestinians were injured, one of them critically, in Israeli gunfire and air strikes across Gaza on Saturday morning, Wafa reported.
Two Palestinians were shot by Israeli forces in displacement camps in the town of Jabalia, north of the Strip, while a woman and a child were wounded after tanks opened heavy fire towards tents for displaced people in the Al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, Wafa said.
Meanwhile, three Palestinians were injured, one of them critically, in an Israeli air strike targeting an area south of Al-Mawasi.
According to Gaza health authorities, more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed and over 6,000 wounded since the ceasefire began in October last year.
